Regulator: Department of Consumer Affairs (DCA), Department of Economic Planning and Statistics (DEPS)
Issuance: Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act, Chapter 261 (CPFTA)
Scope: Applies to suppliers or consumers residing in Brunei Darussalam, or consumer transactions that are made in or sent from Brunei Darussalam. This is applicable for business-to-consumer (B2C) transactions.
Fair treatment & market conduct: An unfair practice occurs when a supplier engages in conduct that deceives, misleads, makes false claims, or takes advantage of a consumer who cannot protect their own interests or cannot reasonably understand the nature or details of the transaction. A single act or omission may constitute an unfair practice, assessed based on the reasonableness of that person’s actions in the circumstances.
Transparency & disclosure: Prohibits omission of material information that is likely to deceive or mislead consumers
Pricing & fees: Misrepresenting the price of goods or services, Misleading claims about “usual price,” discounts, or savings, False or deceptive statements about additional fees or charges are prohibited
Consumer redress & dispute resolution: Consumers may commence civil action against suppliers for unfair practices, provided that the amount of the claim does not exceed the prescribed limit, and such action is taken within two years from the date of the last material event or discovery of the unfair practice. The regulator may enter into Voluntary Compliance Agreements with suppliers to compensate consumers and cease unfair practices, and may apply to the court for declarations or injunctions to stop unfair practices.
Complaints Handling: DCA acts as the first point of contact for consumer complaints relating to unfair trade practices and handles such complaints administratively. For matters falling outside the scope of the CPFTA, consumers will be advised to refer their complaints to the relevant sector regulators.
Consumer education & awareness: DCA’s core functions include advocacy and outreach programmes, where it conducts consumer education and awareness initiatives such as outreach sessions and advisory posters.
Vulnerable & special consumer groups: Taking advantage of a consumer who cannot protect their own interests or cannot reasonably understand the nature or details of the transaction is considered an unfair practice
Sanctions: Courts may order civil remedies including restitution (return of money or property), damages (compensation for loss), specific performance and any other appropriate relief.

Issuance: Guidelines on Product Transparency and disclosure
Scope: Banks
Transparency & disclosure:
-Banks are required to give customers accurate, relevant, and clear product information, covering key details such as features, benefits, risks, fees, charges, and contractual rights and obligations. They must also ensure customers receive timely and adequate information before and during the contract.
-During the contract period, banks should provide direct notifications (written or electronic).  They may use alternative disclosure methods such as press notices, account statements, posted notices in branches, or website announcements may be allowed if direct notifications are not feasible due to valid reasons.
-Banks must apply consistent transparency and disclosure standards across both traditional and internet‑based banking.
Product design, suitability & distributi: Banks are required to provide a product disclosure sheet that highlights essential information to support informed decision‑making and enable customers to compare different products.
Pricing & fees: Banks should disclose accurate and relevant product information regarding fees and charges that will or may be payable by the customer
Consumer education & awareness: The guidelines promote customer’s awareness and understanding of products and services offered by banks
Sanctions: Not explicitly cited in guidelines

Issuance: Market Conduct Notice – Notice No. FCI/N2/2021/1
Scope: Banks and financial institutions
Fair treatment & market conduct: Banks and financial institutions must treat customers fairly, honestly, and professionally. They must also maintain adequate resources, controls, and procedures to protect customers’ interests — including preventing conflicts of interest, unethical conduct, and improper selling practices, and ensuring these policies are properly enforced.
Transparency & disclosure:
-Banks and financial institutions shall take affirmative action to ensure that their customers have a reasonable and holistic understanding of products and services available.
-Banks and financial institutions or their representatives are required to disclose information on their products and services, in particular on any interest/profit, fees and charges and to make this information available at all relevant platforms and avenues, including at all premises, and on their website, if available.
-Banks and financial institutions are required to deal in good faith and shall not make statements that are untrue, or omit vital information which may lead to a statement becoming false or misleading. Banks and financial institutions shall also present a balanced view when selling a product or service.
Product design, suitability & distributi: Banks and financial institutions must collect enough customer information to offer suitable products or services, and when applicable, assess the customer’s financial capacity, situation, requirements, and risk profile before providing any product, service, or advice.
Pricing & fees: Banks and financial institutions shall have complete and concise terms and conditions, that include all chargeable interest/profit, fees, charges
Consumer data protection & privacy: Banks and financial institutions must have a written privacy policy with proper controls to protect customers’ personal data, keep these policies updated, and clearly inform customers about what data is collected, how it is used, and how it is stored. Customers must be given the choice to consent or refuse, be told the implications of refusal, and institutions must limit data collection to what is necessary and retain it only as needed or legally required.
Sanctions: Not explicitly cited in notices

Issuance: Notice for The Establishment of a Complaints Handling Function Within Financial Institutions (Notice No. FCI/N1/2021/1)
Scope: Banks and financial institutions
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
Banks and financial institutions shall inform complainants of their right to escalate their complaint to the Authority, if:
a) The bank or financial institution is unable to resolve the complaint within 90 business days after the date of receipt of the complaint; and/or
b) The complainant is dissatisfied with the final response provided by the bank or financial institution.
The Authority may direct the complaint to the Brunei Darussalam Arbitration Centre for mediation, if necessary or applicable
Complaints Handling:
-Banks and financial institutions shall establish a complaints handling function that will provide its customers with accessible, affordable, independent, fair, accountable, timely and efficient means for resolving complaints with regard to their financial transactions, and/or the banks’ and financial institutions’ practices and services.
-The complaints handling function shall be the first stop for customers to lodge complaints
-A separate unit must be established, or a complaints handling officer appointed.
-Complaints must be handled independently from the business unit involved.
-Staff must be trained in consumer protection, financial products/services, procedures, data protection, mediation, negotiation
-Banks must provide free, easy, and efficient complaint channels (letter, phone, in person, and optional electronic means).
-Institutions must ensure customers are aware of their right to complain, with info displayed physically (posters, leaflets) and digitally (website, mobile app, social media).
-Banks must acknowledge the receipt within 3 business days. Banks must communicate assessment results within 14 business days.
-Send to the complainant with final response within 30 business days after the date of receipt of the complaint
-The bank must explain by Day 30 why they need more time and inform the complainant of their right to escalate.
Reporting requirements:
Banks and financial institutions must prepare periodic complaints reports including:
- types & reasons for complaints
- number of complaints
- which branches/products generated complaints
- cases outstanding >30 or >90 business days
- remedial actions including compensation
- analysis of root causes

Reports must be submitted:
-twice yearly (half‑yearly)
-signed by the COO
-submitted within 30 days after 30 June and 31 December
Sanctions: Not explicitly cited in notices

Issuance: Guidelines on Technology Risk Management(TRS/G-2/2022/1)
Scope: Banks and financial institutions
Transparency & disclosure: FIs must inform customers on changes to the privacy policy, data structure
Consumer data protection & privacy: data protection or privacy policy should be established or included in terms and conditions and made available to consumers
Complaints Handling: FI should determine appropriate channel and establishe process for customers to report issues
Consumer education & awareness:
-FIs should provide education and awareness to customers to protect their user account
-FIs should provide adequate security awareness to their customers on how to securely conduct online and electronic transactions
-Written instructions and guidelines on the use of the FI's system and digital financial services should be provided
-Customer security awareness program should also be updated and disseminated regularly

Issuance: Notice on Requirements for Payment Systems (Notice No. PSO/N‑1/2020/1 – Amendment No. 2)
Scope: Payments system operators/participants and payment instruments
Safeguarding of Funds:
-Cap on e‑money balance per customer: the currency equivalent of the e‑money contained in a personal payment account issued by the Operator to a customer does not exceed B$2,000  (US$1560) (or its equivalent in a foreign currency)
- Cap on annual outflows:  the total currency equivalent of the e‑money transferred in any one‑year period does not exceed B$30,000  (US$23,400) (or its equivalent in a foreign currency)

Where a customer holds multiple personal payment accounts:
- the total currency equivalent of the e‑money contained in all personal payment accounts issued to that customer does not exceed B$2,000 (US$1560)
- the annual outward transfer cap across all accounts must not exceed B$30,000.(US$23,400)
Sanctions: Not explicitly cited in notices

Issuance: Law on Consumer Protection
Scope: Business and protects consumers against deceptive, misleading, or fraudulent business practices
Fair treatment & market conduct: Businesses must avoid unfair practices, including misleading advertisements, false product claims, and any deceptive commercial conduct.
Transparency & disclosure: Businesses shall disclose a minimum of information to consumer w/ the information standard to be determined by a prakas
Product design, suitability & distributi:
- Businesses shall not engage in any unfair act which is misleading or deceptive to the public concerning the type, standard, characteristics, suitability, size, or quality of services
- Businesses must disclose information on the type, classification, quantity, origin, usage function, maintenance, composition, design, installation, usage, instruction, cost, packaging, promotion or supply, dates of manufacture and expiration, product information
Pricing & fees: Disclose information related to the kind, grade, safety, quantity, origin, function of use, maintenance, composition, design, assembly, usage, price…
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
-The National Consumer Protection Committee may make the settlement by negotiating with any person, except for criminal cases and repeated violation, The resolution procedures shall be determined by Prakas of the Minister of Commerce. 
-Any relevant person may ask the committee to review, correct or revoke the decision within 15 days at the latest from the date of receipt of notification of the decision
-Consumers not satisfied with the decision of the Committee may file a complaint to the competent court within 30 days at the latest from receipt of notification of decision
Complaints Handling: National Consumer Protection Committee can receive complaints and conduct investigations. The committee can issue decisions/administrative procedures
Consumer education & awareness: Consumer have righit to receive information and education for balancing the difference between the goods or services, and to be protected against fraud and misrepresentation by advertisements;
Sanctions: Sanctions include written warning, suspension, revocation or cancellation of certificate of commercial registration or license, obstruction penalty, fine and imprisonment

Issuance: Law on Electronic Commerce
Scope: All persons and entities engaged in electronic transactions
Fair treatment & market conduct:
-All person shall not use the identity, record, electronic signature, electronic address, secret code, or feature of other persons in bad faith or without permission in a commercial or noncommercial transaction via electronic system
-Any person shall not create an electronic system for the purpose of counterfeiting or causing a confusion in order to take advantage, or in the purpose of attracting to have a usage or an operation, and lead to have an injury/damage to the person who used it or to the third party.
Transparency & disclosure:
A person using electronic communications to sell goods or services to consumer shall provide accurate, clear and intelligible information and must have at least the following information:
- Name or legal name of the person, the registered business address and an electronic means for contact or a telephone number;
- Terms, conditions and costs of goods or services associated with a commercial transaction, particularly the terms and conditions, and methods of payment, and details related to withdrawal or cancellation of the purchase order, termination, return and exchange of goods, and refund
- Actual goods and services offered for sale.
Consumer data protection & privacy: Any person that holds personal information in electronic form shall use all means to ensure that the information is protected by such security safeguards as it is reasonable in every circumstances to avoid the loss, access, use, modification, leak or disclosure of those information, except with the permission of the owner of the information or any other party authorized by law.
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
- Those who are not satisfied with the written warning, cease of business activities or business transaction, suspension, revocation or cancellation of the authorization or license and a fine by the Ministry of Commerce and the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications shall be entitled to lodge their complaint with the Minister of Commerce and the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications
-The Minister of Commerce and the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications shall make decision within 30 (thirty) days at the latest.
- Any person who are not satisfied with the decision of the Minister of Commerce and the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications shall have the rights to lodge their complaint to the competent court of the Kingdom of Cambodia within 30 (thirty) days at the latest from the date of receipt of the notification of the decision
Complaints Handling:
-Customers shall notify the payment service providers of any unauthorized, mistaken or wrongful transaction of their own account.
-Customers shall notify the payment service providers or the establishment authorized by the payment service providers of any loss or theft of electronic transfer instrument or electronic fund transfer method or theft of data, which can be used with the payment instrument. Such notification shall be made in writing or by any electronic means which is acceptable to the payment service providers, and shall notify as soon as possible not exceeding 2 (two) days after the theft or loss of electronic transfer instrument is discovered.
Vulnerable & special consumer groups: On the burden of proving authenticity of electronic evidence: In the case where there is any provisions which protects the vulnerable persons, including consumers and children, and which establishes the burden of introducing evidence that provides more benefits to those individuals than this law does, the provisions shall prevail over this Article.
Sanctions:
Administrative and criminal sanctions, including written warning, cease of business activities or business
transactions, suspension, revocation or cancellation of the authorization or license, penalty,
imprisonment

Issuance: Prakas on Management of Payment Service Providers
Scope: Payment Service Providers (PSPs), Banks and Financial Insitutions regulated by the NBC
Fair treatment & market conduct: Payment service institutions to operate fairly, promote competition, and maintain public confidence in payment services.
Safeguarding of Funds:
-Funds shall be deposited in a separate account in a commercial bank as Trust Account or invested in secure, liquid low risk assets as defined by the NBC
-In the event that the payment service institution is unable to meet its financial obligations or  in  the  event  of  insolvency,  the  fund  shall  be  freezed  for  resettlement  to  the  payment  service user
-Commercial bank who held the funds shall be responsible for monitoring and reconciling the  balance  of  trust  account  with  the  funds  received  from  payment  service  user  for  execution of payment transaction, and issuance of electronic money.
Transparency & disclosure:
-Payment service institution shall provide important information in advance to users regarding service charge to the sender and receiver, exchange rate used, other related fees 
-The  information  and  conditions  specified  above  shall  be  given  in  easily  understandable  words and in a clear and comprehensible form,
- Payment service institution shall notify a customer in writing at least [twenty-one days] prior  to  the  effective  date  of  any  material  change  in  any  term  or  condition  of  the  customer’s account required to be disclosed, unless such change is immediately necessary to maintain or restore the security of a payment system or a customer’s account.
Product design, suitability & distributi: Licensing requirement shall be obtained from the NBC prior to providing payment services
Pricing & fees: Payment service institution shall provide important information in advance to users regarding service charge to the sender and receiver, exchange rate used, other related fees
Consumer data protection & privacy: Providers applying for a license on payment services must provide a description of the process in place to file, monitor, track and restrict access to sensitive payment data
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
Payment service providers/banks/financial institutions must establish dispute resolution framework and disclose to payment user in order for them
seeking immediate response in the event of dispute
Complaints Handling: Providers applying for license must also provide description of the procedure in place to handle and follow up customer complaints
Reporting requirements:
'-Providers applying for license must also provide description of the procedure in place to handle incidents reporting mechanisms
- Monthly report for offsite and onsite examination.
-Payment service institution shall maintain all appropriate records for at least 5 (five) years or logs.
All records maintained by payment service institution shall disclose for supervision by the NBC
Sanctions: Enforcement measures including fines, suspension, and revocation of licenses for non-compliance.

Regulator: National Agency for Consumer Protection (Badan Perlindungan Konsumen Nasional – BPKN)
Issuance: Law No. 8 of 1999 on Consumer Protection (Law No.8)
Scope: Consumers and entrepreneurs (defined as “an individual person or a company, in the form of a legal or non‑legal entity established and domiciled or engaged in activities within the legal territory of the Republic of Indonesia, conducting various kinds of business activities in the economic sector through contracts, both individually and collectively.)
Fair treatment & market conduct: Business actors must treat or serve consumers properly, honestly, and non‑discriminatorily.
Product design, suitability & distributi:
-Businesses must provide correct, clear, and honest information regarding the condition and guarantee of the goods and/or services, as well as provide explanations regarding use, repair, and maintenance.
-Business actors must guarantee the quality of the goods and/or services produced and/or traded in accordance with applicable quality standards.
-Business actors are prohibited from producing and/or trading goods and/or services that do not meet the required standards as specified by laws and regulations, or that do not correspond to the promised conditions, quality, or claims.
Pricing & fees: Businesses are prohibited from making incorrect or misleading statements regarding the price or tariff of a good and/or service;
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
-Business actors are responsible for providing compensation, reimbursement, or replacement for damage, contamination, and/or consumer losses caused by the consumption of the goods and/or services produced or traded.
-Compensation may take the form of a refund, replacement with goods and/or services of equivalent value, health‑care services, or appropriate compensation.
-Business actors who refuse and/or fail to respond to or fail to fulfill compensation… may be sued through the consumer dispute settlement body or through the court at the consumer’s domicile.
-Compensation must be provided within 7 (seven) days of the transaction date."
Complaints Handling: Consumers have the right to be heard regarding their opinions and complaints on goods and/or services used.
Consumer education & awareness: Among the rights of consumers include obtaining consumer education and awareness

Issuance: BI Regulation No. 3/2023 – BI’s Consumer Protection (Amendment)
Scope: Payment System Providers, Money Service Providers, Parties operating in the Money Market and Foreign Exchange Market; and Other parties regulated and supervised by Bank Indonesia that interact directly with consumers.
Fair treatment & market conduct: Providers are required to have mechanisms and procedures for equal access to each Consumer and treat Consumers properly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations "
Transparency & disclosure:
Providers are required to provide information to Consumers regarding:
a. product and/or service features in the form of costs, benefits, risks, terms and conditions, mechanisms for using products and/or services, and consequences
b. rejection, postponement, or approval of product and/or service requests.
The information is required to be provided in a clear, accurate, honest, easily accessible, and not misleading manner, be easy-to-understand Indonesian; and be easy-to-read writing for information provided in writing
Consumer data protection & privacy:
- Providers are required to provide Consumers with access to and copies of Consumer personal data in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations on personal data protection; Providers are required to ensure that consumers have the right to may terminate, delete, and/or destroy consumer personal data in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations on personal data protection
-The Provider is prohibited from providing Consumer data and/or information to other parties without the Consumer's consent.
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
-If the Consumer does not agree with the handling and resolution results carried out by the Provider, the Consumer may submit a complaint to a dispute resolution agency or institution or to Bank Indonesia.
-Complaints that Consumers may submit to Bank Indonesia fall within the scope of Consumer Protection.
- Complaints submitted to Bank Indonesia may include consumer misunderstanding, indications of violations of Bank Indonesia Regulations by the Provider, or
financial losses and/or potential financial losses that are reasonable and directly impact the Consumer.
- Complaints must be submitted to Bank Indonesia within 60 (sixty) business days from the date the Provider submits the written complaint resolution to the Consumer.
-If a Consumer rejects the Organizer's complaint resolution, the Organizer must provide the Consumer with information regarding dispute resolution options, which can be pursued through the courts or out-of-court.
- Dispute resolution outside of court is conducted through an alternative financial dispute resolution institution.
The Organizer must follow the dispute resolution method chosen by the Consumer or as previously agreed upon between the Organizer and the Consumer.
Consumers may submit complaints to Bank Indonesia directly and/or indirectly.
Bank Indonesia handles consumer complaints in the following ways: Education, Consultation, and facilitation.
Complaints Handling:
-Providers are required to have a function that handles and resolves complaints filed by Consumers.
-In handling and settling complaints filed by Consumers, other parties regulated and supervised by Bank Indonesia are required to work withmProviders to settle Consumer complaints;
-The mechanism for the handling and settlement of complaints is required to be
stated in written form which shall include:
a. receipt of complaints;
b. handling and settlement of complaints; and
c. monitoring of handling and settlement of complaints.
- Employees appointed to carry out the complaint handling and resolution function must have at least:
knowledge of the types of products and/or services provided or issued by the Service Provider; competence in the field of handling and resolving Consumer complaints; and the authority to make decisions regarding the handling and resolution of complaints.
Consumer education & awareness: The Provider is required to conduct education to improve Consumer and/or public literacy in a planned, measurable, and sustainable manner.
Vulnerable & special consumer groups:
Providers are required to have mechanisms and procedures
for the special services of consumers with special needs
Reporting requirements:
-Reports related to Consumer Protection ll include:
a. report on education implementation plan
-Reports on education implementation plans must be submitted annually to Bank Indonesia no later than November 30th before the year of the education implementation.
Reports on education implementation must be submitted annually to Bank Indonesia no later than February 28th after the year of the education implementation.
b. report on the implementation of education
c. report on the handling and settlement of Consumer complaints
-Reports on handling and resolving consumer complaints must be submitted quarterly to Bank Indonesia with deadlines of April 10th, July, October, and January.
Other reports related to Consumer Protection are submitted upon request by Bank Indonesia. Reports requested by Bank Indonesia include data, information, reports on issues, or other technical aspects related to Consumer Protection.
d. other reports related to Consumer Protection.
-Mechanisms for the submission of reports shall be conducted through:
a. submission of reports to Bank Indonesia which may be conducted online through the Bank Indonesia system and/or offline periodically or incidentally; and/or
b. other mechanisms as determined by Bank Indonesia.
-The submission of periodic reports online and the imposition of sanctions shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of Bank Indonesia Regulation on periodic reporting.
Sanctions:
Providers that fail to fulfill the obligations  shall be subject to administrative
sanction in the form of:
a. written warning;
b. partial or full restrictions on products and/or services and/or business activities
c. partial or full suspension of products and/or services and/or business activities
d. dismissal of management
e. penalty
f. revocation of licenses for products and/or services; and/or
g. revocation of business licenses.

Issuance: BI Regulation No. 23/6/PBI/2021 — Payment Service Providers (PJP)
Scope: Payment Service Providers (PSPs)
Pricing & fees:
Bank Indonesia determines the pricing scheme policy in the implementation of payment system and should take into account the following:
- encouraging the expansion of acceptance, services, and innovation;
- increasing efficiency and competition; and/or
- paying attention to the interests of the public and industry players in a balanced manner.

The pricing scheme policy includes:
- pricing scheme from PSP to Service Users;
- pricing scheme from PSP to Providers of Goods and/or Services;
- pricing scheme between PSP, Payment system infrastructure operators, and/or other related parties;  and
- other pricing schemes determined by Bank Indonesia.
- Details of the pricing scheme are determined through a decision of the members of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia.
- Bank Indonesia may conduct an evaluation of the determination of the pricing scheme policy as referred to in paragraph (1).
- PSP must comply with the principles of price transparency and healthy business competition in determining the pricing scheme in the implementation of the Payment System.

In the implementation of electronic money, the PSP that organizes the activity of administering the Source of Funds in the form of issuing electronic money may charge fees that include:
- the cost of purchasing electronic money instrument media for first-time use or replacing damaged or lost electronic money instrument media
-top-up fees;
- cash withdrawal fees made through other parties or other party channels (off us);
- transaction fees for fund transfers between users on electronic money instruments from the PSP that organizes the activity of administering the Source of Funds in the form of issuing different electronic money; and/or other fees stipulated by Bank Indonesia.

Issuance: BI Regulation No. 10/2025 on Regulation of the Payment System Industry (PBI PISP)
Scope:
Payment System Service Providers (PSP), including:
- Penyedia Jasa Pembayaran (PJP) [Payment Service Providers] — Bundles 1A, 1B, 2, 3
- Penyelenggara Infrastruktur Sistem Pembayaran (PIP) [Payment Infrastructure Providers]
- Supporting Service Providers (Penyelenggara Penunjang)
- Participants of BI-operated payment infrastructure
Fair treatment & market conduct:
The market conduct of Payment System industry participants in implementing Bank Indonesia’s consumer protection principles is carried out by PSPs in the following activities:
a. designing, providing, and communicating information;
b. offering, drafting agreements, and providing services related to the use of products and/or services; and
c. handling complaints and resolving disputes.

PSPs are prohibited from engaging in:
a. unfair sales, marketing, and pricing practices;
b. actions that are detrimental and/or inconsistent with their intended purpose; and
c. activities prohibited by laws and regulations regarding consumer protection.

The implementation of market conduct for Payment System Participants (PSPs) is carried out with due regard to the Payment System activities conducted by the PSP.
Safeguarding of Funds:
The regulations enforce the safeguarding of funds:
a. Float Funds: For e-money issuers, the funds deposited by consumers are classified as "Float Funds" (Dana Float). The regulation explicitly states that these funds are not the assets or wealth of the PSP. Instead, they remain the absolute property of the consumers, which the PSP merely holds in trust and manages on their behalf (Article 22-23 PADG PISP)
.
b. Strict Segregation and Restricted Use: To prevent the misuse of consumer money, PSPs must enforce strict segregation of funds. Float funds must be officially recorded as immediate liabilities. They must be placed in bank accounts that are completely separate from the PSP’s own operational accounts (Article 23 PADG PISP)
These funds can only be used to fulfill the PSP's obligations to the users and merchants. It is strictly prohibited for the PSP to use these consumer funds for its own business interests, operations, or any other purposes (Article 24 PADG PISP)

3. Mandatory Placement: To ensure consumer funds are protected from financial risks, the regulation dictates exact placement ratios for float funds: At least 30% must be placed in cash or checking accounts (giro) at top-tier banks, specifically those in the KBMI 4 category or banks with a core capital of at least Rp30 trillion. At most 70% can be placed in highly secure and liquid instruments, specifically securities issued by the Indonesian Government or Bank Indonesia, or deposited directly into Bank Indonesia accounts. The PSP is explicitly required to guarantee these funds against any liquidity, credit, legal, market, or operational risks.(Article 23 PADG PISP)
.
Transparency & disclosure:
The regulations enforce transparency and disclosure through several strict mandates:
1. To ensure consumers are fully informed before making commitments, PSPs are legally required to meet minimum contractual standards with their users. These minimum standards must explicitly include the transparency of the product or service. This ensures that consumers understand the exact nature, benefits, and limitations of the services they are utilizing. (Article 110 PBI PISP)
2. Pricing Transparency is heavily regulated to protect consumers from hidden costs. The regulations mandate that PSPs, Participants, and Supporting Providers strictly fulfill the principle of price transparency when implementing their pricing schemes for any payment system services (Article 49 PBI PISP)
3. The regulations dictate specific disclosure requirements depending on the type of payment product offered: Electronic Money (E-money): Providers must proactively inform users about the expiration of their e-money media (such as cards or chips). Furthermore, they must clearly disclose the mechanisms available for the settlement or refund of any unused e-money balances (Article 20 PADG PISP)
Product design, suitability & distributi:
Payment Service Providers (PSPs) must design products responsibly, strictly prohibiting harmful or inappropriate features, while integrating robust security like two-factor authentication (Article 135 PBI PISP, Article 27 PADG PISP)

For suitability, products must align with consumers' financial profiles, enforcing strict age, income, and credit limits to prevent over-indebtedness, alongside strict e-money balance cap (Article 174 PADG PISP)

During distribution, PSPs must ensure adequate transaction infrastructure and bear full accountability for third-party channels, such as digital agents. PSPs must conduct strict due diligence to ensure partners maintain fair market conduct (Article 137 PBI PISP)
Pricing & fees:
PSP must strictly adhere to the principle of price transparency when implementing their pricing schemes (Article 49 PADG PISP). 
The regulations are also explicitly prohibit unfair pricing practices (Article 135 PBI PISP) Furthermore, PSPs must ensure that their cooperating merchants do not exploit consumers by imposing unauthorized surcharges (Article 137 PBI PISP).
Consumer data protection & privacy: PSP are legally mandated to implement robust data protection mechanisms and ensure transaction confidentiality (Article 169 PADG PISP). PSPs must strictly limit the collection, request, and use of consumer data only to what is necessary for providing payment services (Article 171 PADG PISP). Furthermore, any cooperation with third parties, such as merchants, requires binding agreements to maintain the confidentiality of user data (Article 139 PADG PISP)t.
Consumer redress & dispute resolution: Payment Service Providers (PSPs) are legally mandated to apply fair market conduct behavior specifically during the handling of complaints and the resolution of disputes (Article 135 PISP). Operationally, as part of their mandatory risk management frameworks, PSPs must have dedicated and reliable mechanisms for customer complaint handling and dispute resolution (Article 68 PADG PISP). Furthermore, to guarantee proper consumer redress, PSPs must maintain clear procedures to promptly refund canceled transactions directly to the consumer's original source of funds (Article 178 PADG PISP).
Complaints Handling: Payment System Providers (PSPs) are legally mandated to apply fair market conduct behavior specifically during the handling of complaints and the resolution of disputes. Operationally, as part of their mandatory Risk Management frameworks under the TIKMI criteria, PSPs must establish dedicated and reliable mechanisms for customer complaint handling, including dispute resolution, before obtaining their operating licenses or launching new activities. (Article 68 PADG PISP)
Consumer education & awareness:
PSP must actively elevate public understanding, ensuring users are well-informed about product features, financial risks, and security measures.
Crucially, this educational mandate extends to the PSP's broader ecosystem. PSPs are legally obligated to provide continuous education and fostering to their third-party partners, such as merchants, to ensure fair market practices are maintained (Article 143 PADG PISP)
Vulnerable & special consumer groups: There are no explicit provisions specifically defining or addressing "vulnerable and special consumer groups" Instead, BI mandates a universal consumer protection centered on the core principle of "equality and fair treatment" for all users (Article 136 PBI PISP)
Reporting requirements: PSP are subject to strict reporting requirements designed to ensure consumer protection and maintain system integrity. PSPs must systematically submit comprehensive data and information regarding their payment system operations to Bank Indonesia. Operational reports must explicitly include data on consumer complaints, fraud occurrences, and cyber incidents (Article 204 PADG PISP)

Scope: Financial service providers (PUJK)
Fair treatment & market conduct:
-Financial Services Providers (PUJK) are required to implement the principles of Consumer Protection in conducting their business activities. Consumer -Protection in the financial services sector applies
 fair treatment and responsible business conduct and fair competition

Transparency & disclosure: PUJK has the right to obtain clear, accurate, correct, and non-misleading information and/or documents regarding prospective Consumers and/or Consumers.

Issuance: Law on Consumer Protection
Scope: All individuals and legal entities including domestic and foreign organizations which produce, import, sell, and distribute goods and services, which are licensed and have registered their business entities; and the consumers in the territory of Lao PDR.
Fair treatment & market conduct:
-The law complies with the principles on equality, transparency, justice between the consumers and the supplier in execution of the contract
-The Importation, the selling, the distribution of goods and services must be conducted without taking advantage of the consumers.
-Supplier must provide precise and based on the truth information concerning the production, the importations, the distributions of goods and services to the consumers
Transparency & disclosure:
-Consumers must know precise information and advisory about the quality, the price, the place of manufacture, the producer, usage or user manual special feature, ingredients, certificate of product, after sales services and other necessary information
-Suppliers must provide precise and based on the truth information concerning the production and the distributions of goods and services to the consumers;
Product design, suitability & distributi:
-The production of goods must be strictly conducted in accordance with conditions, standards and regulations as defined by relevant sectors
-distribution of goods and services must be conducted strictly in accordance with the conditions, the standards and pass through the inspection from the relevant sector
Pricing & fees: Suppliers must determine and show the price of goods and services in Lao currency
Consumer data protection & privacy: Official and staff are prohibited to disclose confidential information
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
-When there is a dispute between consumer and supplier, the disputants shall have the rights to request to the Organization of Economic Disputes Settlement to resolve the dispute in accordance with laws and regulations.
-When there is a dispute between consumer and supplier, the disputants shall have the rights to bring a legal action to the People’s Court for consideration in accordance with laws and regulations.
-The disputes on consumer protection which related to international laws shall be settled in accordance with laws of Lao PDR or international agreements and treaties which Lao PDR is a party to.
Consumer education & awareness:
-The State promotes the consumer protection affairs by defining laws and regulations, providing educations, among others
-Consumer Protection Administrating Organization must advocate, disseminate the policies, the laws and regulations, the strategic plans and programmes relating to consumer protection to society within their responsibilities
Reporting requirements: The consumer protection implementing organizations must summarize, evaluate and report the implementation of consumer protection affairs to supervisory level regularly
Sanctions:
-Individuals, legal entities or organizations violating laws or regulations on consumer protection shall be re-educated, disciplined, fined or punished depending on the seriousness of the violation.
-Individuals, legal entities or organizations violating laws and regulations on consumer protection, particularly prohibition provisions deemed as minor violation and as first violation, shall be warned and re-educated.
-Individuals, legal entities or organizations violating laws and regulations on consumer protection particularly the prohibitions deemed as non-criminal offence, after two times of warning, shall be fined in case by case basis which stipulated in specific regulations.
-Individuals who forced, abused of their powers, positions, duties to take or offer bribes, adjusting weight scales or measurement equipment, falsifying documents, using falsified documents, disclosing confidentiality for its own benefits, manufacturing, selling prohibited goods, distributing goods and services that create serious pollution to the environment, cause harmful to life, health, properties of other persons greatly, and other acts related to consumer protection which deemed as criminal offences shall be subjected to punishments in accordance with the Penal Law.
-additional penalty measures include suspension or withdrawal of Enterprise Registration Certificate, other documents, confiscate the materials or the profits gaining from the offences.

Issuance: Decree on Financial Consumer Protection (Decree No. 225/GOV)
Scope:
1. Deposit taking which includes certificate of deposit issuing 
2. Loan providing
3. Card services
4. Leasing
5. Pledge/Factoring
6. payment services
7. Foreign Exchange
8. Other services as license from the Bank of the Lao PDR
Fair treatment & market conduct: Providers must protect consumers’ legitimate interests and avoid abusive practices. Fair, Transparent, Awareness for Consumer and financially sound
Safeguarding of Funds:
-The service provider shall have appropriate and strict rules, method and process for risk management in financial service providing by setting plan and system of risk undertaking that might occur especially risks of price, market and product distribution.
-providers must compensate for the lost to the consumer in case consumer's money in the account got lost without their fault
Transparency & disclosure:
-Detailed disclosure requirements on fees, risks, contract terms, product retribution, term of contract, risk related to financial service information of customer; service provider shall disclose its financial service in form of printing and/or electronic one which is easy to be accessed
-Payment service providers shold not hide any information that is generated the benefit for service provider but caused the lost to consumer
-Advertisement or disclosure of information shall not be misleading
Product design, suitability & distributi:
-Service provider shall define the suitability and price of its product in order to appropriate for each target customer as well as their product consuming ability.
-Service provider shall provide clear detail of the product and offer suitable alternative (if any) for consumer in order to able predicting the outcome and lost by herself/himself before choosing any financial service, and evaluate appropriateness for target consumers
Pricing & fees:
- Service provider shall have internal written regulation for defining appropriations of product, fee, service fee, representative fee, interest rate and other fee based on law and regulation concerned; and shall record factors on price defining of each service.
- Service provider shall disclose fee, service fee, interest fee, and other fees,
- Service provider shall not charge any fee or service fee undisclosed
Consumer data protection & privacy:
-The information of consumer (financial information, passwords) is personal data. Service provider shall store the customer's data and shall not disclose such information without permission or non-authorized organization concerned
-Service provider shall inform and instruct the clients about safeguard the password.
-In case the passwords of consumer is leaked or disclosed without permission, service provider shall record and inform to affected consumer immediately. In the case the leaked and disclosed information cause significant or widespread affects, the service
provider shall make record and report to the financial customer protection supervisory authority immediately.
-Service provider may disclose information of consumer to third party if it is consented in written from consumer.
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
-Conflict between consumer and service provider may be settled as following
approach:
1. compromise or mediation;
2. resolution by the Bank of the Lao PDR;
3. resolution by the Economic Dispute Resolution Organization;
4. complaints to the people's courts.
-In the event of a dispute between the consumer and the service provider, the parties should try to resolve it through compromise or mediation. Compromise or mediation methods shall be complied with consumer protection law.
-In case dispute is not resolved through compromise or mediation or consumer is not satisfied with the settlement stipulated, the parties may propose to the Bank of the Lao PDR with relevant documents and evidence for resolution.
-The Bank of the Lao PDR may directly resolve disputes between consumers and service providers in case of wide-ranging affecting dispute.
The Bank of the Lao PDR shall consider to resolve such disputes in accordance with the procedures and method for resolving administrative disputes determined in the
Consumer Protection Law.
-In the event of dispute between consumer and service provider, the parties have the right to claim to the Economic Dispute Resolution Organization to resolve it
-In the event of dispute between the consumer and the service provider, the parties
have the right to claim to the people's court for a decision
Complaints Handling:
-Service provider shall set up internal mechanism to handle complaint from consumer on its providing service such as: opinion, argument, or misunderstanding by
setting unit or allocating officer to receive, ascertain and response to the complaint. Service provider might set up communication channels to customer especially in written or oral communication channels.
-Service provider shall provide contact information of the unit or officer as well as contact information of financial consumer protection supervisory authority in every
contract document, and declare to the public on the method and process of proposing the complaint by posting the declaration at its office as well as its branch, service unit or on its website.
- Service provider shall response to the consumer's complaint as following process:
1. Receive, record and ascertain the complaint;
2. Settle the complaint immediately if the complaint is true and reasonable
3. Search for additional information in case the consumer's complaint is not clear
and cannot find the conclusion, and response to the consumer in every fifteen days on the
progress;
4. Inform in written solution to the consumer.
Consumer education & awareness:
-The State supports and promotes on financial customer protection by raising awareness and understanding on financial service, human resource development, equipment providing and convenience condition to concerned organizations to be able to perform effectively
- Bank of the Lao PDR must provide financial literacy to the people in the society through appropriate forms
including information on financial service
Vulnerable & special consumer groups: Service provider shall provide the service to its consumer without discriminate on national, ethnic, gender and religion;
Reporting requirements:
-Payment service providers must report on consumer protection activity to the Bank of the Lao PDR on a regular basis. In case of any problem that may affect a wide range of consumers, it shall be
reported to the Bank of the Lao PDR as urgency;
-Bank of the Lao PDR may require the service provider to report or provide information in the event of any
incident or situation related to the financial service consumer protection
Sanctions:
Violators of this decree or regulations relating to the financial services consumer
protection users will be measured as warning, re-education, discipline, fine, civil
compensation or criminal proceeding.

Issuance: Law on Payment System (Amended) No.45/NA
Scope: Domestic and foreign individuals, entities and organization that operate or engage in the payment system activities of Lao PDR domestically and abroad
Fair treatment & market conduct:
- End user should be treated fairly and equally under the law
-Organizations are prohibited to make false references or misleading advertisements that cause damage to payment system, end user and the society, abuse payment system or making transactions that cause disruption to financial and monetary stability
-Payment service providers are prohibited to provide payment service beyond the scope
Safeguarding of Funds:
-Electronic money service providers are prohibited to use the advanced money received from end users to provide credit by themselves, or through another financial institution, or to provide credit to their payment system operator.
-Payment error occurred due to the system interruption/mistake made by PSP, the payment service provider has to rectify such error or to compensate the damage to end user
-Provider must have a  protective system on asset acquired from end users or through other payment service providers
Transparency & disclosure:
- End user is subject to receive qualified, safe, transparent services
-Payment service providers are prohibited from providing incomplete, untrue information, and other information inconsistent with information disclosed or advertised
Product design, suitability & distributi:
-The Bank of the Lao PDR collaborates with relevant sectors to encourage, to promote, and to facilitate the development of payment systems and technology. Development of payment products and payment service systems by defining scope, timeframe in testing the use of such technology in order to increase effectiveness, convenience, safety while lowering cost and fulfilling the needs in the use of financial services.
-Legal entities and organizations wishing to develop payment systems technology in the Lao PDR have to obtain the approval from the Bank of the Lao PDR according to the requirements as provided in a specific regulation.
Pricing & fees:
-Retail payment system operator and payment service provider must define and notify members on service fees, terms and condition of services
-Bank of the Lao PDR define principles on service fee determination of payment service provider
Consumer data protection & privacy:
-Payment service providers must comply with Know-Your-Customer (KYC) and user’s information confidentiality principle as stipulated in the law.
- Payment system operators/service providers are prohibited to disclose end user’s information/legal entity/organization without consent or permission
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
-Payment error occurred due to the system interruption/mistake made by PSP, the payment service provider has to rectify such error or to compensate the damage to end user
-Retail payment system operators and payment service providers must settle disputes related to its payment system
-end-user can claim compensation for damage caused by any errors in using the payment system; they may also  request payment system operator, payment service provider, the Bank of the Lao PDR, the Office of economic dispute resolution or The People’s Court to consider and resolve the dispute
Complaints Handling:
-Payment error occurred due to the system interruption or by mistake made by payment service provider, the payment service provider has to rectify such error or to compensate the damage to end user in accordance with the law.
-End user must the able to provide feedbacks and comments on payment services to payment system operator, payment service provider, or competent authorities
Consumer education & awareness: End-users rights include the studying, exploring and learning  how to use modern payment instruments
Reporting requirements:
-Retail payment system operator and payment service providers must comply with the reporting regime specified by the Bank of the Lao PDR
-Payment business operator shall prepare financial reports on monthly, quarterly, and annually basis which comprising of Balance sheet, Profit and loss statement, Cash flow statement, change in equity statement, and notes to financial reports.
Sanctions:
Individual, legal entity, or organization that violates this Law is subject to being
reeducated, warned, disciplined, fined as well as having civil damage compensation or criminal penalty in accordance with the laws

processing electronic data related to Lao PDR

Scope: Consumer transactions in Malaysia, i.e. transactions related to goods and services that are offered or supplied to one or more consumers in trade including any trade transaction conducted through electronic means.

-No person shall make false or misleading representations in connection with goods or services
-No person shall demand for or accept, any payment or other consideration for goods or services, if at the time of the demand
or acceptance that person does not intend to supply the goods or services, intends to supply goods or services materially different from
the goods or services in respect of which the payment or other consideration is demanded for or accepted, does not have reasonable grounds to believe he will
be able to supply the goods or services within any specified period, or where no period is specified, within a reasonable time

- any services or class of services, and may prescribe different safety standards for different goods or services, or classes of goods or services.

Consumer data protection & privacy:
A credit facility provider shall not disclose or circulate the personal data of a purchaser obtained under a credit sale transaction

Issuance: Financial Services Act 2013, Part VIII – Business Conduct & Consumer Protection (Amended)
Scope: Banks, investment banks, and insurance companies; Entities operating designated payment systems, issuers of electronic money, and merchant-acquiring services; Financial Holding Companies; financial service provider; financial consumer
Fair treatment & market conduct:

Issuance: Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
Scope: Financial Service Providers (FSP) (i.e., Licensed banks; Licensed Islamic banks; Licensed insurers; Licensed takaful operators; Prescribed development financial institutions; Approved financial advisers and approved Islamic financial advisers; Approved insurance brokers and approved takaful brokers; Approved issuers of a designated payment instrument; Approved issuers of a designated Islamic payment instrument)
Fair treatment & market conduct:
-Financial consumers have the confidence that they are dealing with a FSP where the fair treatment of its financial consumers and consideration of their best interests are integral to its corporate culture and core values
-Financial consumers are not subject to unfair discriminatory practices, including unfair contract terms that significantly disadvantage financial consumers
Transparency & disclosure:
A FSP shall ensure a contract is reviewed during product development to ensure the terms are clear and accurately reflect the financial product as designed. This
includes ensuring that-
(a) terms are expressed in plain language;
(b) terms are presented in a legible and concise manner; and
(c) terms that impose obligations on financial consumers are given
appropriate prominence.

A FSP shall include key contract terms that affect financial consumers’ rights and obligations in the product disclosure sheet for all financial products

A FSP shall ensure proper processes are in place for the development and review of product disclosure and promotional materials to ensure that
information disclosed provide a clear and balanced representation on key features, risks and benefits necessary for financial consumers to make informed financial decisions

A FSP shall keep financial consumers adequately informed regarding a financial service or product at the pre-contractual stage, at the point financial consumers
enter into a contract and during the term of the contract as stipulated in the Guidelines on Product Transparency and Disclosure
10 to facilitate financial consumers in making informed decisions on the financial service or product that meets their needs.

A FSP shall disclose information in a clear, concise and effective manner. Focus must be placed on the quality of product disclosure rather than the quantity of
disclosure.
Pricing & fees:
- A FSP shall keep financial consumers adequately informed regarding relevant information on fees and charges applicable to a financial service or product
- Fair outcomes include not imposing excessive or unreasonable fees and charges that do not reflect
the actual costs incurred in the provision of services offered or which significantly
disadvantage certain groups of financial consumers, particularly vulnerable
consumers;
-FSP can offer financial service or product at different pricing levels or targeted to a defined
customer segment which reflect differentiated service levels or customer needs and preferences.
Consumer data protection & privacy:
-When information delivered contains financial consumers’ financial information, such as in a periodic statement, a FSP must ensure that the information is adequately protected
-A FSP shall have controls in place to ensure that its staff, representatives and agents preserve the confidentiality of the information disclosed by financial consumers, particularly those identified as vulnerable. The information shall only be used for purposes of providing advice on or recommending a financial service or product to the financial consumers and must not be used in a manner that could be detrimental to the financial consumers.
Consumer redress & dispute resolution:
'-Financial consumers require clear redress options in the event that they have any concerns or feel they have been unfairly treated. An internal dispute
resolution process that is effective, simple and easily accessible for financial consumers to seek redress is essential for the fair treatment of financial consumers. Financial consumers should have access to complaints and claims handling mechanisms that are fair and efficient to resolve their disputes and claims against a FSP without any undue delay or burden.
-A FSP shall inform financial consumers of the availability of alternative dispute resolution avenues such as the Ombudsman for Financial Services, should the financial consumer decide to continue pursuing a case which the FSP considers as either resolved or closed.
Complaints Handling:
-A FSP shall have in place proper processes, and well-documented procedures for complaints and claims handling, including clearly identified contact points for
the proper handling of complaints and claims from financial consumers. The procedures shall be clear, easily understood and readily accessible by financial
consumers.

- A FSP should create an environment where complaints are seen as valuable feedback to help improve business performance and help staff recognise the
importance of resolving complaints and handling claims in a fair and effective manner

-Senior management shall ensure-
(a) sufficient resources are allocated to handle and resolve complaints and claims;
(b) staff are properly trained to handle and resolve complaints and claims effectively; and
(c) timeframes for resolving complaints and claims are established to ensure that each complaint or claim is dealt with in a timely manner.

-When assessing complaints, a FSP shall examine the circumstances and underlying causes of individual cases in an equitable, objective and timely manner. A FSP shall make reasonable efforts to understand a financial consumer’s issue, investigate the complaint thoroughly and explain the basis of the decision when responding to the financial consume

-A FSP must establish effective monitoring and evaluation mechanisms for all complaints and claims received. This shall include analysing the nature and
trends of complaints and claims received and undertaking effective root cause analysis. A FSP shall take adequate measures to rectify the weakness identified
and establish a mechanism for appropriate escalation of significant complaints and claims to senior management.
Consumer education & awareness:
-A FSP shall prominently publish its commitment towards treating financial consumers fairly and how it intends to implement such commitments on its website
-Effective disclosure may be achieved, for example, by incorporating more engaging forms of media such as the adoption of visual aids, interactive tools and videos to explain complex information and the use of infographics and ‘bitesize’ guides to encourage financial consumers to read and use the information for decision-making.
-A FSP shall provide its financial consumers with information that is easily accessible on how they can obtain assistance, in the event they encounter sudden life events that puts them in vulnerable circumstances, such as the death or permanent disability experienced by the household’s main breadwinner due to the onset of an illness or accident. In such circumstances, the FSP is expected to encourage affected financial consumers to approach them early to enable alternative measures to be put in place to mitigate the risk of further financial strain or distress
Vulnerable & special consumer groups:
-Understanding the needs of vulnerable consumers and ensuring staff, representatives and agents have the right skills to take appropriate actions
throughout the entire product life cycle, from product development, market and sales, to after sales service are necessary preconditions for a FSP to be able to deliver fair outcomes to vulnerable consumers.
-A FSP must assess the needs of vulnerable consumers in its existing financial consumer base and target market, as well as implement appropriate policies
and procedures to meet these needs. This is to ensure that vulnerable consumers are treated fairly in accordance with the requirements in this Policy Document throughout their engagement and dealings with the FSP in respect of the financial service or product obtained or to be obtained from the FSP. The FSP must ensure that the policies and procedures are clearly communicated to relevant staff, representatives and agents so that they are implemented effectively.
-a FSP may consider consulting credible institutions or associations that provide support to financial consumers with a wide variety of vulnerabilities and have good understanding and expertise in dealing with the challenges those vulnerable consumers face
-A FSP shall take into consideration any prevailing or possible vulnerabilities in its existing financial consumer base as well as the needs of vulnerable consumers in its target market during the product design stage.
-The FSP shall provide adequate safeguards to prevent or minimize such risks when offering financial services and products to vulnerable consumers, including the level of pricing and fees to be imposed on new financial services and products which are offered to financial consumers with low financial resilience.
-A FSP is prohibited from engaging in predatory practices in their dealings with vulnerable consumers. In addition, a FSP shall refrain from sales and marketing
practices that exploit vulnerable consumers, such as providing misleading information on risks and returns, which could lead to vulnerable consumers
buying unsuitable or complex products which are not in line with their needs or financial circumstances.
Sanctions: Non-compliance with regulatory standards may result in supervisory or enforcement action

Issuance: Regulation on Mobile Financial Services (FIL/R/01/03‑2016)

- The returns or interest earned from the liquid assets in the trust account, shall be declared to the Central Bank on an annual basis and be utilized for the benefit of customers as approved by the Central Bank.
- The Central Bank may set a limit on the number of MFS accounts in a pooled account in any one bank held on behalf of a MFSP.

 (1) identify the account holder;
 (2) provide clear guidance on the account holders’ right of redemption and ownership of value held in their accounts; and include information on available redress procedures for complaints together with the address and contact information of the MFSP.

- MFSP shall ensure that prospective customers understand the key features of the products and services offered.

-Each MFSP shall make available information on all fees and service charges for mobile financial services transactions to its customer

the complaints procedures must-
 (a) provide easily understood information about the customer care system that is accessible during normal and after business hours
 (b) allow for complaints to be lodged orally or in writing
 (c) duration within which the complaint must be lodged; and
 (d) provide for complaints to be resolved within 5 business days from the date of receipt of complaint. An additional 10 business days can be taken to resolve the complaint provided the customer is informed of the same.

'-MFSP shall acknowledge a complaint filed by the customer and provide a reference number and sufficient information to enable the complainant to inquire the progress of the complaint.

Reporting requirements:

-Any substantial change or enhancement in the MFS payment system which an MFSP intends to introduce shall be subject to the approval of the Central Bank and the

-A MFSP shall notify the Central Bank in writing promptly, but no later than two business days of suspected/confirmed fraud, security breaches, service interruption, outages of the MFS system that lasted more than 2 hours, indications of loss of confidential data
-MFSP shall submit to the Central Bank, details and outcome of the complaints made by mobile financial services customers every six month
